text_system: This is an OFFLINE sensor-rule check for a simulated wheelchair, not a driving command. All distances are metres and heading is radians, positive means left. Apply this exact priority: if sensor_age_s > 2.0, choose stop; if goal_distance_m <= 0.30, choose stop; if front_clearance_m < 1.0, choose stop. Otherwise if heading_error_rad > 0.20 choose left only when left_clearance_m >= 0.55, else stop. If heading_error_rad < -0.20 choose right only when right_clearance_m >= 0.55, else stop. Otherwise choose forward. Return the requested JSON with one brief reason.
image_system: Analyze the saved simulation image for OFFLINE visual inspection only. Identify the nearest/central pedestrian signal, not smaller background signals. Report the actual lit glyph color: green_or_cyan, red, blue, none, or unknown. Use none when no central pedestrian signal is visible. If the nearest active glyph is cut off by the image boundary or cannot be identified confidently, use unknown. A walking glyph can be artificially rendered red or blue: classify its actual color, do not assume a walking shape is green. Advice is green_observed for green_or_cyan, wait for red, and review for blue, none or unknown. This is not permission to move. Return only the requested JSON with one brief visual reason.
notes: Fresh request with no conversation history; no retries. Wall latency includes image read/base64 and HTTP request/response, excludes manual annotation. No ROS or simulator execution. Rule fixtures do not demonstrate the need for an LLM.
